title: Katavi National Park: Tanzania's Most Remote Park
excerpt: Katavi, in western Tanzania, is one of the most remote parks in Africa. For travellers who want true wilderness and huge herds of buffalo and hippos.
body:
Katavi National Park lies in western Tanzania, far from the main safari routes. Very few people visit, which is exactly its appeal.

## The dry season spectacle

In the dry season the rivers shrink, and wildlife concentrates around the remaining water. Large buffalo herds and crowded hippo pools are the signature sights.

## Wildlife

Buffaloes, hippos, crocodiles, elephants, lions, leopards, giraffes, zebras and many antelope.

## Wilderness

There are only a few camps. You may spend a day without seeing another vehicle.

## Getting there

Usually on scheduled light aircraft flights, which run only on certain days. It is often combined with [Mahale](/blog/mahale-mountains-chimpanzees/) or Ruaha.

## When

Best from roughly June to October. In the wet season the park is largely inaccessible and camps close.

## Who it suits

Experienced safari travellers who want something truly remote. See also [your second safari](/blog/second-safari-ideas/).

Read our [Katavi page](/national-parks/katavi-national-park/) or [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
